mechanistic_conclusions: Whole-table deletion is first an A/public-locator failure under the current exact-table-count locator contract.
One-tail-segment y truncation can leave the locator at rank 1 while preventing deterministic V18 from producing any candidate payload; V20 is therefore not the responsible repair layer.
When localized shape-preserving numeric damage still produces a candidate payload, the tested V20 outcome continues to match the declared per-shard RS byte-error capacity with zero mismatches.
Adding RS parity cannot fix the observed whole-table-deletion or tail-truncation failures without first changing the upstream structural locator/parser behavior.
boundaries: This is a bounded 24-seed synthetic experiment, not a universal physical-publication robustness claim.
Only one deterministic target-table rule and the declared deletion/truncation/burst families were tested.
The 4-vs-6 segment burst result is evidence for the existing fixed V20 geometry, not proof that 6.25% parity is optimal.
B/r structural corruption and broader table insertion/reordering/multi-table loss are not characterized here.
